terroir.title: Quinta da Touriga-Chã
terroir.subtitle: Schist, sun, and the Douro Superior.

soil.title: The Schistous Soil
soil.text: Pre-Cambrian schist — fractured, vertical plates of metamorphic rock that force vine roots deep into the earth. This ancient geology provides extraordinary drainage, forcing the vines to struggle and concentrate flavour.

climate.title: The Climate
climate.text: The Douro Superior enjoys over 3,000 hours of sunlight annually — among the highest in Europe. Diurnal temperature shifts of up to 20°C preserve natural acidity while allowing full phenolic ripeness. The Marão and Montemuro mountain ranges shelter the valley from Atlantic influence, creating a continental microclimate of extremes that forges wines of power and finesse.

expression.title: The Expression
expression.text:
The fractured schist bedrock lends a distinctive mineral identity, while the intense Douro sunshine fosters concentration, complexity, and depth. Together, they shape wines of great aromatic intensity, impressive structure, and refined elegance. They are a true reflection of the Douro Superior, expressing a unique sense of place that exists nowhere else in the world.

These wines are distinguished by their extraordinary ageing potential, evolving in complexity, elegance, and depth over decades.

viticulture.title: Viticulture
viticulture.subtitle: Safeguarding the genetic heritage of the Douro through integrated, sustainable production. Every vine planted with intention. Every root system a direct connection to the fractured schist below.
viticulture.text: The vineyard is planted predominantly to Touriga Nacional — the variety José António was the first to champion as Portugal's finest. Low yields, high density, and a philosophy of minimum intervention allow the personality of each parcel to speak without interference. The result is fruit of extraordinary concentration and aromatic precision.

facts.label: Grape varieties
facts.value: 80 % Touriga Nacional · 20 % Tinta Roriz / Touriga Francesa

vinificacao.title: Winemaking
vinificacao.subtitle: The transformation from grape to wine is an act of custodianship, not creation. The fruit arrives at the winery and is treated with the reverence it commands.
vinificacao.text: Fermentation in small lagares and temperature-controlled stainless steel. Ageing in French oak barrels, used with subtlety to refine tannins without masking the fruit. The goal is transparency — a wine that tastes of its vineyard, its vintage, and nothing else.

adega.title: The Winery
adega.subtitle: Built in 2004, the adega is an architectural statement of intent. Designed with intentional false symmetries, it blends raw functionality with award-winning aesthetic integration into the Douro valley.
adega.text: Concrete, schist, and light. The building follows the contour of the land, sinking into the hillside to maintain a constant temperature. Gravity-flow design minimises pumping. Every decision — from the orientation of the fermentation hall to the depth of the barrel cellar — serves the wine.

familia.title: The Family
familia.subtitle: Six generations. One valley. An unbroken thread of dedication to the Douro.
familia.text: José António Castro Ramos Pinto Rosas (1919–1996) — founder of ADVID, co-creator of modern vineyard systems, and revered internationally as the Pioneer of the Douro. At 72, he found a virgin 20-hectare property near Vila Nova de Foz Côa and planted 8.5 hectares from scratch, with over 80% Touriga Nacional. Today, his son Jorge Rosas, the fifth generation, continues that legacy from the award-winning 2004 winery.

jarpr.name: José António Rosas
jarpr.text: Founder of ADVID. Co-creator of modern Douro vineyard systems. Portugal's representative at L'Office International du Vin. Founder of the Confraria do Vinho do Porto. Known internationally as the Pioneer of the Douro. At 72, he planted 8.5 hectares from scratch — his final and greatest project.

bio.title: José António Ramos Pinto Rosas
paragraphs: José António Rosas devoted his entire professional career to the Port and Douro Wine industry and to the world's oldest demarcated and regulated wine region, the Douro Valley. His remarkable contribution to the development and modernization of the region earned him recognition from leading international wine writers, who referred to him as the “Douro Pope” (as described by Chantal Lecouty in Le Porto, page 145), the “Prophet of the Douro”, and the “Pioneer of the Douro”.

Throughout his career, José António Rosas played a decisive role in shaping the modern Douro wine region. His work was always guided by a single objective: to improve both the quality of Port and Douro wines and the efficiency and sustainability of vineyard production systems.

Among his most significant achievements was the development of the patamares vineyard planting system, which facilitated vineyard mechanization while adapting to the region's steep slopes. Together with his nephew, João, he also pioneered the introduction of vertically planted vineyards (vinha ao alto), a revolutionary approach that allowed greater mechanization, higher planting densities, and improved grape quality through lower yields per vine. This extensive research into grape varieties and rootstock selection laid the foundations for many of the viticultural practices that are now widely adopted throughout the Douro Valley.

José António Rosas also represented Portugal at the Office International de la Vigne et du Vin (OIV), was a founding member of the Confraria do Vinho do Porto (Port Wine Brotherhood) and served as Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of Ramos Pinto, one of Portugal's most prestigious Port and Douro wine producers.

Driven by his unwavering commitment to raising the quality standards of Douro wines, he founded ADVID (Association for the Development of Douro Viticulture) in 1982. Under his leadership as President until 1996, ADVID became one of the most respected viticultural research institutions in Portugal.

José António Rosas was also co-author of The Port Wine, a reference work published by the Instituto dos Vinhos do Douro e do Porto (IVDP), further cementing his legacy as one of the most influential figures in the history of the Douro and Port Wine industry.

jorge.name: Jorge Rosas
jorge.text: Son of José António. Steward of the Quinta da Touriga-Chã since his father's passing. Built the award-winning 2004 winery. Continues the legacy with the same uncompromising dedication to the Douro, its vineyards, and its wines.

sixth.title: The Sixth Generation

people.name: João Rosas
people.text: João began his career in global management consulting firm advising multinational corporations and private equity portfolio companies on operational improvement and value creation initiatives. He holds an MBA from Saïd Business School, University of Oxford, where he was a Dean’s List recipient, and a Bachelor's degree in Industrial Economics from the University of Nottingham. He is currently an Associate at Headway Capital Partners, a London-based private equity investment firm. João is fluent in English, French, Spanish and Portuguese.

people.name: José Maria Rosas
people.text: José Maria holds a Master in Finance from ESCP Business School, ranked the world's No. 1 Master in Finance by the Financial Times, and a degree in International Management with Finance from the University of Warwick. He gained experience in private credit and acquisition finance before joining LGT Capital Partners in London. Fluent in English, French, Spanish and Portuguese, he founded the Warwick Wine Society and holds a WSET Level 2 certification.

people.name: Jorge Rosas
people.text: Jorge is currently pursuing a BSc in Management at Nova School of Business and Economics, one of Europe's leading business schools. He graduated with highest honours from the Lycée Français International de Porto, ranking among the top 10% of students worldwide in the French Baccalauréat. Fluent in Portuguese, English, French and Spanish. He supports his father in various aspects of the estate's operations.

sixth.closing: Together, João, José Maria and Jorge represent the sixth generation of the Rosas family, combining a heritage deeply rooted in the Douro Valley with experience and education acquired at some of Europe's leading universities and financial institutions.

quinta.title: The Quinta da Touriga
paragraphs: After dedicating more than fifty years of his life to viticulture in the Douro Valley, and only a few years before his passing, José António Castro Ramos Pinto Rosas decided to fulfil a lifelong dream: to create the “dream estate” to produce exceptional Port and Douro wines.

Following an extensive and detailed study of the region, supported by topographic maps and decades of experience, José António Rosas identified a 20-hectare property in the Douro Superior, near Vila Nova de Foz Côa, with all the characteristics required for producing top-quality wines, including ideal altitude, exposure, and soils.

In the early 1990s, at the age of 72, he acquired the property and set out to apply all the knowledge he had accumulated throughout his career. Starting from scratch, he planted 8.5 hectares of vineyards, carefully selecting grape varieties best suited to the local climate and the region’s challenging schist soils. No vineyards had ever been planted on the property before.
His pioneering decision to plant a vineyard with more than 80% Touriga Nacional led him to name the estate Quinta da Touriga.

Despite its naturally low yields, José António was among the first visionaries to recognise Touriga Nacional as one of Portugal’s finest red grape varieties and its greatest potential for producing world-class wines.

Today, Quinta da Touriga encompasses approximately 40 hectares and is managed by José António’s son, Jorge Rosas, the fifth generation of a family dedicated to wine production. In 2004, Jorge built a state-of-the-art winery, further elevating the estate’s ambitions. The wines produced at Quinta da Touriga have since been widely recognised by leading Portuguese and international wine critics and writers as among the finest wines produced in Portugal.
